## 裁决 — 不可重裁 (维护者 2026-08-25, #11663 comment 5404675670, verbatim「接受你的建议，继续」, bundle 1A/2B/3A/**4A**/5A/6A/7A)

- `ensure-default-organization` **re-pointed**, and its **trigger moved** (design H4 — a fourth id-shaped read of a different *kind*: population, not predicate, so #10348-C as specified does **not** absorb it).
- The post-#10348-C judge **reads the same oracle as core's derivation** — ⛔ no second derivation site; the 4A posture branch lives inside the one site.
- **`last-admin-guard` re-pricing is its OWN reviewed step** (migration step 5).

## ⛔ The single hardest constraint on this card

⛔ **Do not delete or add guard refusals as a side effect of the re-pointing commit.** With no runtime write able to empty the platform-admin population, several refusals become obsolete and several become newly necessary — but that re-pricing is a **separate, reviewed change**, and the card says so in terms.

⇒ Practically: keep the re-point and the re-pricing as **distinct commits** with the second one arguable on its own. And **every deleted or added guard refusal must be enumerated in the PR body with its re-pricing rationale** — that is an acceptance criterion, ⛔ not a courtesy.

## ⚠️ This card now also owns an interim window L4 opened

From L4's review: the **out-of-repo enterprise organizations package** reuses `ensureDefaultOrganization`, which still finds the admin via **grant rows** and triggers on grant inserts. A **fresh walled rig** on that package will not auto-create its default organization between L4's landing (now done) and this card's re-point.

⇒ **That window is open right now**, and closing it is this card's. In-repo paths were measured unaffected (`plugin-auth`'s bootstrap is gated `!postureEnforcesWall`). ⚠️ Your re-point must not assume the out-of-repo caller's shape — if the re-point would break it, **say so**; that is a coordination item, not something to guess at.

## PM mechanism assumptions — measure these; I would rather be falsified

1. **That the trigger move is separable from the re-point.** The card lists them together (H4). If moving the trigger forces the re-pricing early, ⛔ stop and report rather than folding the reviewed step into the re-point commit — that is the one thing the card forbids.
2. **That `single`-posture behaviour is genuinely unchanged.** Choice 4A keeps first-user promotion and its grant row. **Pin it**, and make the pin one that would go red if the re-point leaked into the `single` branch. ⛔ An "unchanged" claim without a pin is an assumption.
3. **That the walled-rig acceptance is reachable here.** The criterion is *"walled bootstrap end-to-end per the design §2 flow passes on a walled rig"*. If that needs a rig this repo cannot stand up, **say which half you verified and which needs an operator** — ⛔ do not let a green unit suite stand in for the end-to-end criterion. ⚠️ This lane has two cards stuck on exactly that conflation.

## Gates

Re-derive from **your** worktree at `origin/main` and your **actual** diff: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs <changed paths>`. ⚠️ **Read BOTH sections of its output** — the path-derived block *and* the whole-tree kind-gates section. Two devs tonight each dropped one section with an extraction grep and each was reddened in CI by a family the tool had in fact named (#13642).

## Report

Terminal report as a comment on this issue **first**, then as your return message. Machine-checkable fields only. **Enumerate every guard refusal touched, with its rationale** — that is a required field here, not the PR body's alone.

**PM verdict (`domain:services` seat, #6021) — L3 delivery ACCEPTED. This card stays OPEN; here is exactly what is left and who reads it.**

Carrier: **PR #13685** (draft, `needs:contract-review`), head `df17ff0a7`. My independent verification of the card's fences is posted on the PR — the short form: the two reviewed steps really are two commits (`be6e37144` re-point / `de9db6593` re-pricing), the re-pointing commit touches **no guard file**, and every one of the 41 changed lines in `last-admin-guard.ts` is a comment (non-comment diff filter returns empty; `throw` census 6→6). The card's ⛔ — *do not delete refusals as a side effect of the re-pointing commit* — held, and the acceptance criterion's enumeration is of an empty set in code, with the set arithmetic's re-pricing pinned in both directions (4 now-permitted, 5 still-refused, including the *declared-but-unverified* over-relaxation control).

## Disposition of the three acceptance clauses

| clause | status |
| --- | --- |
| every deleted/added guard refusal enumerated with rationale | ✅ **MET** — verified independently, above |
| `single` posture behaviour unchanged (Choice 4A) | ✅ **MET** — the four "still refused" counter-pins plus the config-UNSET zero-read assertion are the leak detector for exactly this |
| walled bootstrap end-to-end per design §2 passes on a walled rig | ❌ **NOT MET, and not claimable from this repo** |

## The two halves that keep this card open

**(a) The out-of-repo trigger adoption → filed as #13689.**
The enterprise organizations package reuses `ensureDefaultOrganization` with its own wiring on `sys_user_permission_set` inserts, which post-L4 never fire on a fresh walled rig. L3 **shrank** that window from "forever" to "until the next process start" (their `kernel:ready` pass now resolves a config-anchored admin, because L3 re-pointed the population and did not change the signature) — but it did not close it. Closing it needs their wiring to import the newly exported `isDefaultOrganizationBootstrapTrigger`.

⛔ That fix lands **outside this repo**, which has no `repo:*` lane for it (`repo:enterprise` does not exist in this repo's label set) and is outside the session's GitHub scope, so file-at-destination cannot be executed by this seat. #13689 is therefore the objectstack-side seam anchor with **named readers** (this seat; and the maintainer/director seat, who must route the enterprise-repo half). It is not the implementation.

**(b) The walled-rig end-to-end pass — no vehicle in this repo's harness.**
The criterion needs a live walled rig with a real registration + verification round trip. Every step of the §2 flow that is unit-pinnable is green (population, trigger set, guard prices, `single`-posture invariance), and I am recording explicitly that **⛔ those green unit suites are NOT the end-to-end pass and must not be allowed to stand in for it** — the dev delivering L3 flagged this rather than claiming it, which is the correct call. The in-plan vehicle is the **L6 reap card #11978** ("reader census on a walled rig"); an operator run is the alternative.

## Next state transition (recorded now so it is not re-derived later)

While #13685 is open this card stays `pm:dispatched`. **When #13685 merges**, this card flips in one write to `pm:blocked` + `Blocked-by: #13689` — ⛔ **not** closed by the merge, and the PR is correctly marked `Part of` rather than a closing keyword (the "Part-of PR must not also close its card" check is green on it). Full closure additionally needs (b): either #11978's rig or a maintainer ruling that the end-to-end pass is satisfied by other evidence. Neither is this seat's to decide unilaterally.

⛔ Not done and deliberately so: no `pm:retriage`, no re-dispatch. The delivery is complete for everything reachable from this repo; the remainder is coordination and rig access, not code.

**Pointer — ADR-0131 C1 (#15195) now owns half of this card's surface.** Not a re-ruling of this leg; a collision notice so the two do not each land a half.

ADR-0131 (merged 2026-09-04, #14976) makes `ensure-default-organization` a **boot invariant** under `single`: its failure becomes a boot error rather than a best-effort warning, and its **trigger moves earlier** — before `SeedLoaderService.load` runs and before the first authenticated request — because from v18 every seed row must be stamped with an organization that therefore has to exist first (D3, D9, D11). That is card **#15195**, and it re-points the same function this leg's content line re-points.

**What that does and does not settle here:**

- ✅ The **re-pointing and the trigger move** are absorbed by #15195. Whoever dispatches that card reads this one first; whoever dispatches this one after #15195 lands will find the re-pointing already done and should say so rather than redo it.
- ⛔ The **`last-admin-guard` re-pricing** — this card's own second half, and explicitly "its own reviewed step" — is **not** touched by ADR-0131. It survives this card intact. ⛔ Do not read the absorption above as this card being finished.

This card stays `pm:blocked` on its existing upstream. It is **not** moved behind the v18 gate (#15193): its remaining half is not ADR-0131 work and must not inherit ADR-0131's staging.

Refs: ADR-0131 D3/D9/D11 · #15195 (C1) · #15194 (execution tree) · #15193 (the v18 gate — for context only; this card is not behind it).

**Coordination half closed.** The seam card #13689 is closed as completed — verified today rather than assumed:

- `packages/plugins/organizations/src/organizations-plugin.ts:492` calls `isDefaultOrganizationBootstrapTrigger`, and cloud's copy does the same at `:446`. `git log -S` shows the framework path only ever saw `c677cda81`, so the code arrived already fixed — cloud had adopted the predicate before PR #16215 (ADR-0132) copied the package into open core verbatim. The report back here simply never happened.
- The control clause #13689 insisted on separately — *not* "it works after a restart" — is `walled-default-org-self-registrant.pin.test.ts`, which names that seam card in its header and asserts `the bootstrap really IS registration-triggered here — a 'sys_user' insert reaches the helper`, paired with a positive control on the operator's declared address verifying.
